question: Which cells in the stomach lining make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?
explanation: Spot on! Parietal cells are the stomach's acid factories. They also make intrinsic factor, which your body needs to absorb vitamin B12 properly. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the main job of chief cells in the stomach?
explanation: You got it! Chief cells release pepsinogen, which stomach acid turns into pepsin to help break down the proteins you eat. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which common bacterium is a major cause of long-term gastritis and stomach ulcers?
explanation: Well done! Helicobacter pylori (or H. pylori) loves to hang out in the stomach lining, causing irritation and stubborn ulcers over time. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h2)

question: A patient with long-term chronic gastritis is most at risk for lacking which vitamin?
explanation: Exactly! When gastritis damages the stomach's parietal cells, you lose intrinsic factor, meaning your body can't absorb vitamin B12 like it should. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h2)

question: How does stomach pain from a gastric ulcer usually behave compared to a duodenal ulcer?

options.A: Gastric ulcer pain often worsens soon after eating food.
options.B: Gastric ulcer pain is relieved by eating meals.
options.C: Duodenal ulcer pain gets worse immediately during a meal.
options.D: Duodenal ulcer pain never occurs at night.

explanation: Correct! Food triggers acid release, which immediately irritates a gastric ulcer. Duodenal ulcers, on the other hand, often feel better temporarily when food is in the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which serious complication of a peptic ulcer causes a hard, board-like abdomen and severe pain?
explanation: Spot on! If an ulcer burns right through the stomach wall, stomach contents leak into the belly, causing a medical emergency with a very rigid, painful abdomen. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is an early warning sign often reported by someone developing stomach cancer?
explanation: You got it! Feeling full very quickly after eating a small meal (early satiety) along with mild, ongoing indigestion can be an early hint of stomach trouble. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is stomach cancer often found at a late stage?

options.A: Diagnostic imaging tests cannot visualize the inner stomach lining.
options.B: Tumors in the stomach grow much faster than in any other organ.
options.C: Early symptoms closely mimic common, benign stomach issues like gastritis.
options.D: Patients routinely refuse endoscopy procedures until they bleed.

explanation: Exactly! Because early signs look just like normal heartburn or mild gastritis, people often brush it off until the tumor grows larger. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the best diagnostic test for looking directly at stomach ulcers and taking tiny tissue samples?
explanation: Well done! Passing a tiny camera down (endoscopy) lets the doctor see the stomach lining directly and take samples for tests. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h5)

question: After a patient has an upper endoscopy, what is the most important nursing check before giving them water?

options.A: Administering a large meal immediately to test stomach tolerance
options.B: Checking for active bowel sounds every fifteen minutes
options.C: Keeping the patient flat on their back for at least six hours
options.D: Confirming that the patient's gag reflex has returned before offering fluids

explanation: Spot on! The throat spray numbs the back of the throat, so we must wait for the gag reflex to come back to prevent them from choking on water. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h5)

question: How do proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) help treat peptic ulcers?

options.A: By blocking the enzyme system responsible for acid secretion
options.B: By killing all bacteria residing in the digestive tract
options.C: By neutralizing stomach acid the moment it enters the gut
options.D: By coating the entire stomach lining with a sticky barrier

explanation: Correct! PPIs turn off the tiny acid pumps in the stomach lining, drastically cutting down the amount of acid produced so the ulcer can heal. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do doctors prescribe multiple antibiotics at once to treat an H. pylori infection?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing common side effects
options.B: To speed up the healing time of the skin across the abdomen
options.C: To prevent the bacterium from developing resistance to single drug therapies
options.D: To replace the intrinsic factor lost during chronic inflammation

explanation: You got it! H. pylori is tough, so combining drugs stops the bacteria from outsmarting a single antibiotic and clears the infection completely. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do we advise patients with peptic ulcers to eat smaller, more frequent meals?

options.A: It prevents large fluctuations in gastric acid secretion and stomach distension.
options.B: It speeds up the rate at which food empties into the large intestine.
options.C: It completely cures the bacterial infection without needing antibiotics.
options.D: It ensures that the liver produces enough bile for fat digestion.

explanation: Spot on! Small meals keep the stomach from stretching too much and stop huge waves of acid from flooding the stomach all at once. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h7)

question: A patient goes home after treatment for a bleeding gastric ulcer. Which symptom should they report to the nurse immediately?

options.B: A slight increase in morning appetite

explanation: Well done! Black, tarry stools mean there is digested blood coming from higher up in the gut, which can be a sign of dangerous bleeding. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h7)
